The present writ petition has been filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India r/w Section 482 Cr.PC. praying for grant of parole to the petitioner for a period of four weeks.

sentences.text: When the matter was listed on 08.11.2023, the sister of the petitioner appeared in-person and stated that since their own house is in dilapidated condition, she is staying on rent in the same locality and the address of the said residence was furnished by her to the Investigating Officer.
The address where the petitioner's sister is presently residing, now stands verified by the Investigating Officer and a status report dated 09.11.2023 in this regard has been filed.

8. To be noted that the petitioner is in custody for last almost fourteen years including the remission earned.
9.

The purpose of parole as listed out in Rule 1200 of the Delhi Prison Rules, 2018 reads as under:
"1200.

The objectives of releasing a prisoner on parole and furlough are:
i. To enable the inmate to maintain continuity with his family life and deal with familial and social matters, ii. To enable him to maintain and develop his self-confidence, iii. To enable him to develop constructive hope and active interest in life, iv.
To help him remain in touch with the developments in the outside world, This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 13/11/2023 at 21:18:19 v.

To help him remain physiologically and psychologically healthy, vi. To enable him to overcome/recover from the stress and evil effects of incarceration, and, vii. To motivate him to maintain good conduct and discipline in the prison."
10. Clearly, the very purpose behind grant of parole is to enable the prisoner to redeem and rehabilitate himself.

As per the scheme of parole under Delhi Prison Rules the offenders who demonstrate a commitment to reconcile with the society and whose behaviour shows that they aspire to live as law-abiding citizens are to be encouraged by granting a parole so that he could maintain his family and social contacts.

11. Coming back to the facts of the case, on an earlier occasion also petitioner's application for parole was rejected by the Competent Authority on similar ground that the petitioner was re-arrested in another case FIR No. 361/2020 under Section 363/376 IPC and Section 6 of POSCO Act registered at Police Station Prem Nagar, Delhi.

However, on writ petition being filed by the petitioner,
direction was issued by this court to grant parole to the petitioner for a period of four weeks vide order dated 18.10.2022 passed in W.P.(Crl.) 1324/2022.
12.
It is not in dispute that when the petitioner was granted parole vide order dated 18.10.2022, he did not misuse the liberty granted to him.

A perusal of the nominal roll which has been handed over in court today and is taken on record, shows that the Jail conduct of the petitioner during last one year has been satisfactory and he has also been working as langar sahayak.

opennyai_summary.decision:
On an overall conspectus of facts and circumstances, the petition deserves to be allowed.
Ordered accordingly.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 13/11/2023 at 21:18:19 that the petitioner be released on parole for a period of four weeks from the date of his release subject to his furnishing a Personal Bond in the sum of Rs. 10,000/- and one surety bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Jail Superintendent, further subject to the following conditions:
a) he shall not leave NCR region without informing the local SHO;
b) he shall reside at the residence of his sister, the address of which has been furnished to, and verified by, the IO.
c) he shall provide his own as well as his surety's mobile number(s) to the Jail Superintendent and the same will be kept operational at all times;
d) he shall commit no offence whatsoever during the period he is on bail;
and e) he shall report to the Police Station Prem Nagar, Delhi on every Monday and Saturday at 10.00 A.M. during the period of parole.
14.
Upon expiry of period of four weeks as stated above, the petitioner shall surrender before the Jail Superintendent.
15. The petition is allowed, in the above terms.
